slot.brief: Combustion analysis or reaction of a compound: given masses of products, find the mass of an element or moles of a reactant consumed

stem: A compound contains 40.0% carbon, 6.7% hydrogen and 53.3% oxygen by mass. Its molar mass is $180\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$. The molecular formula of the compound is
notes: from question bank gaa6accdf42cc (verified in job 20261127-115414-780e)
working:
Assume 100 g: C = 40/12 = 3.33 mol; H = 6.7/1 = 6.7 mol; O = 53.3/16 = 3.33 mol. Ratio C:H:O ≈ 1:2:1 → empirical formula CH₂O, empirical mass = 30. n = 180/30 = 6 → C₆H₁₂O₆.

Independent check: For 100 g: C:H:O ≈ 3.33:6.7:3.33 ≈ 1:2:1, giving empirical formula CH₂O (30 g mol⁻¹). The molecular formula is (CH₂O)₆ = C₆H₁₂O₆.
solution:
For 100 g of compound, the mole ratio is $\frac{40}{12}:\frac{6.7}{1}:\frac{53.3}{16} \approx 1:2:1$, so the empirical formula is $\mathrm{CH_2O}$ (molar mass $30\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}$).\\
$$n=\frac{180}{30}=6,\qquad (\mathrm{CH_2O})_6=\mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6}.$$
